profile.reading:
This facility in Alpharetta, Georgia, part of the Atlanta metro area, is currently operated by STACK Infrastructure, which identifies it as campus ATL01 on its own website: two buildings, ATL01A at 8 megawatts across 105,000 square feet and ATL01B at 12 megawatts across 133,000 square feet, together totaling 20 megawatts of IT capacity across 238,000 square feet on 18 acres, explicitly stated by STACK to be powered by Georgia Power. The underlying source data for this record carries the name "T5 Data Center," which does not appear anywhere on STACK's current site for this or any other location. T5 Data Centers is a real, separate, currently operating data center developer, confirmed via its own website, claiming more than 3 gigawatts of managed power capacity across facilities it has developed since roughly 2008, but T5's own current site makes no claim to any Alpharetta property. The most plausible explanation for the name/operator mismatch in this record is that T5 originally developed this building before it came under STACK's current ownership or operation, a common pattern in the data center industry where map and property records retain a legacy developer's name after an ownership change, but that specific lineage could not be independently confirmed from any source reached this session, and is flagged here as an open question rather than asserted as settled fact. Alpharetta itself is an established secondary Atlanta-area technology and telecom corridor. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities at ATL01 are not publicly disclosed, and no street address or year of completion is stated on STACK's public site for this campus.

T5 Data Centers, the name attached to this OSM record, describes itself as a developer with more than 3 gigawatts of managed power capacity and roughly 4 million square feet developed across 22 data centers since its founding around 2008, and disclosed in a September 2, 2026 announcement that its construction business is being spun off as an independent entity called EverOn DCS while its operations business transitions to a company called Salute, a corporate restructuring unrelated to this specific Alpharetta building but relevant to understanding T5's current status as a company.
profile.research_note: This OSM record carries the name "T5 Data Center" but STACK Infrastructure's own current site identifies its Alpharetta, GA campus as ATL01 (2 buildings, ATL01A 8MW/105,000 sqft and ATL01B 12MW/133,000 sqft, totaling 20MW/238,000 sqft on 18 acres, powered by Georgia Power), with no reference to T5 anywhere on STACK's site. T5 Data Centers is confirmed via its own website (t5datacenters.com) to be a separate, real, currently operating company (3+ GW managed capacity claimed, founded circa 2008), whose own site makes no current claim to any Alpharetta asset. A T5-built-then-STACK-acquired lineage for this specific building is a plausible explanation for the "name vs operator" mismatch in the source OSM data (a common real-estate pattern where the original developer's name persists as a map label after a change of operator) but could NOT be independently confirmed this session -- flagged honestly rather than asserted as fact. T5 also announced a corporate restructuring around 2026-09-02 (construction spun off as "EverOn DCS," operations business transitioning to "Salute"), unrelated to this specific building but noted for currency.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's Alpharetta campus, designated ATL01, comprises two buildings totaling 238,000 square feet on 18 acres with 20 megawatts of IT capacity. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, this represents roughly 500 racks; at 10 kilowatts per GPU equivalent, roughly 2,000 H100-class accelerators. The facility is powered by Georgia Power and sits in an established Atlanta-area technology corridor.

This campus ranks fifth by published capacity among Georgia's four facilities with disclosed megawatt figures, representing 30 percent of the state's 66.3 megawatts of published IT load. Georgia itself has 33 mapped data center locations, though most publish no specifications. The state context suggests limited visibility into total capacity; published figures capture only a fraction of actual regional infrastructure.

The campus's relevance to AI scaling depends on power reliability and grid headroom at Georgia Power's Atlanta footprint, neither of which is published here. Stack Infrastructure operates the asset as of September 2026. Tenant identities, completion date, and any certifications qualifying the site for GPU-intensive workloads are not disclosed.
